title: Genomic Resources and Modern Breeding Strategies for Lentil (Lens culinaris Medik.) Improvement: Current Advances and Future Perspectives
content: Lentil (Lens culinaris Medik.) is an important grain legume worldwide, valued for its nutritional properties and its contribution to sustainable agricultural systems through biological nitrogen fixation. Conventional breeding strategies in lentil have primarily focused on increasing yield, improving resistance to biotic and abiotic stresses, enhancing seed quality, and optimizing plant architecture. The combination of biotechnological and genomic tools with conventional breeding approaches has accelerated genetic improvement and expanded the possibilities for crop improvement. Quantitative trait locus (QTL) mapping has facilitated the identification of genomic regions associated with quantitative traits, providing valuable information for marker-assisted selection (MAS) and enabling more targeted selection of genotypes. Genome-wide association studies (GWAS) have further contributed to the identification of genetic variants and genomic regions associated with agronomically important traits. Genomic selection (GS) offers additional opportunities to improve selection efficiency, particularly for complex traits. CRISPR/Cas9-based gene editing is a promising emerging technology for crop improvement; however, its application in lentil remains limited, partly due to challenges associated with transformation, tissue culture, and plant regeneration. Speed breeding (SB) can accelerate genetic improvement by reducing generation time and increasing the number of generations per year, and its combination with phenomics and genomic data may improve breeding efficiency. Therefore, cooperation between emerging technologies and conventional plant breeding offers new opportunities to accelerate genetic improvement in lentil while also presenting technical, biological, and regulatory challenges that need to be addressed. This review highlights current advances, remaining limitations, and future perspectives for integrating modern breeding technologies into lentil improvement programs.
